title: Pilot listing: mini criteria and UX copy lab
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc is a bite-sized, pragmatic checklist + copy lab for a small pilot listing (target: SMB ISV partner) that we can ship quickly to a single cloud marketplace tile (AWS or GCP). Aim is to reduce back-and-forth with partner legal and infra while keeping customer-facing copy tight and measurable.

Quick goals for pilot: 
- Produce a marketplace tile and one-sentence hero + 2 short bullets + 20–40 word description.
- Validate billing SKU mapping and metering story with finance + cloud.
- Complete minimal security/compliance gating (KMS note, data residency) so partner can launch in US + EU.
- Timebox: 3 sprints (6 weeks) from kickoff to publish.

UX copy sketch (hero, bullets, short description):
- Hero option A (value-first): "Redwood Inference — predictable LLM inference for production apps"
  - Bullet 1: "Low-latency text generation and embeddings with transparent per-token pricing"
  - Bullet 2: "SLA-backed dedicated capacity and private deployment options for regulated workloads"
  - 20–40 word description: "Run LLMs at production scale with a single API and predictable economics. Choose hosted, reserved, or private deployment modes with tools for routing, caching, and cost optimization."

- Hero option B (outcome-first): "Ship LLM features faster — predictable latency, lower unit cost"
  - Bullet 1: "Plug-and-play API for chat, generation, and embeddings"
  - Bullet 2: "Model-aware routing and caching to minimize cost without compromising quality"
  - Short description: "Redwood Inference helps engineering teams deliver reliable, cost-conscious LLM features across hosted and private environments. Backed by performance tooling and enterprise controls."

Microcopy variants (for A/B later) — short CTA ideas:
- "Start free trial" / "Try now — free credits" / "Request demo" / "Get a dedicated quote"

Marketplace acceptance checklist (minimum viable for pilot):
1) Technical acceptance (platform):
   - Tile artifacts: hero title, short description (20–40 words), 2 bullets, logo (SVG 280x120), feature screenshot (PNG, 1200x628) — done
   - Container/endpoint integration doc: sample API call, token auth steps, region availability — drafted
   - Billing SKU mapping: SKU id + metering unit, free-credit promo mapping, trial period — finance sign-off required
   - Metrics & logging: top-level metrics we can show on tile (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens) — add anonymized numbers

2) Security & compliance (minimal pilot):
   - Data handling note: "no customer data persisted outside session KV cache" (if applicable) — security review pass
   - KMS integration: mapping for customer-managed keys is optional for pilot; require doc note and contact for next phase
   - Privacy: region availability statement (US, EU); add link to privacy policy — legal ok'd

3) Legal & partner requirements:
   - Marketplace T&Cs acceptance: partner must complete listing agreement (link) — owner: partner success
   - Trademark & brand guidelines: logo usage file + short alt text — design check
   - Liability/billing thresholds: include clear refund/credits policy for metered billing — legal draft included

4) Product & GTM prep:
   - One-pager for sales and partner success with FAQ + troubleshooting steps (internal) — draft
   - Support playbook: how to troubleshoot common issues (auth, rate limits, billing disputes) — SRE and PS input needed
   - Onboarding flow: sign-up → API key issuance → quickstart prompt templates (3 examples)

Acceptance gates (must be green to publish pilot):
- Platform: tile assets uploaded and validated in sandbox; test API calls succeed in 3 regions (us-west, us-east, europe-west)
- Billing: SKU mapped and metering validated in sandbox billing; finance approves trial credit allocation
- Security: security review has no open high/critical findings; KMS doced for future opt-in
- Legal: partner/marketplace listing agreement signed or legal issues scoped with timeline
- Support: on-call rota defined for first 30 days post-launch

Risk & mitigation quick notes:
- Risk: Billing SKU edge-cases (metering mismatch) — Mitigation: add a 14-day grace/credits window for any misbilled customers, communicate proactively
- Risk: Performance expectations mismatch — Mitigation: include per-route latency guidance in tile and link to runbook; enable canary fallback to smaller model variant
- Risk: Partner delays on legal assets — Mitigation: ship tile with "Coming soon: enterprise features" and limit geos if necessary

Implementation tasks (owner quickmap):
- Product (Sofia): finalize hero copy + short description, assemble tile assets (logo, screenshot) — week 1
- Design (Liam): production-ready tile images + accessible alt text — week 1–2
- Engineering (Ethan): sandbox endpoint validation, region smoke tests, sample quickstart repo PR — week 1–3
- Finance (Priya): SKU creation, billing sandbox validation, define trial credit amount — week 2
- Legal (TBD): review legal blurb + refund policy — week 2–4
- Support/PS (TBD): build one-pager and on-call plan — week 3

Notes to partner success (short):
- Keep messaging tight: customers on marketplaces scan quickly — hero should promise one specific operational outcome (latency, cost, or security).
- Avoid detailed product architecture in tile copy; link to docs for deep dives.
- Collect two measurable signals in pilot: 1) tile CTR → lead conversion, 2) trial-to-paid conversion for customers who hit >X API calls.

Follow-ups / questions for next sync:
- Decide primary CTA (trial vs request demo) based on SMB vs mid-market target segment.
- Confirmation of trial credit USD amount (finance).
- Do we include a short "how it works" 3-step graphic on the tile or keep it off-tile and in docs?

Slack threads / tickets to reference: 
- slack: #mkp-launch (thread: pilot-slate-2026) 
- jira: GTMP-1191 (pilot listing integration)
- pr: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-tiles/pull/234

Quick editorial checklist (pre-publish):
- [ ] Plain-language hero tested with 3 PMs 
- [ ] Accessibility alt text verified 
- [ ] Billing SKU validated in sandbox 
- [ ] Legal blurb uploaded and linked 
- [ ] Support on-call rotas scheduled

This is intentionally lightweight and pragmatic — the goal for the pilot is to learn fast about demand signals and friction in the listing flow. If we get healthy conversion and low legal/billing friction, we then expand into multi-region and upgrade the tile copy to include enterprise features and dedicated capacity callouts.

End of doc.
